# Lists

Functions over lists. None of them mutate their input: `sort` and `reverse` return new lists. Functions that take a lambda accept an implicit `.` lambda or an arrow lambda, and call it with the item and its index.

Every function can be called as `f(x, ...)` or as a method, `x.f(...)`. In the signatures, `T` and `U` stand for any type, `T[]` is a list, `?` marks an optional parameter, and `(T, number) => boolean` is a lambda parameter.

The examples use this context:

```ts
const context = { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] }
```

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`map`](#map) | Transforms each item. |
| [`filter`](#filter) | Keeps the items for which the lambda is true. |
| [`find`](#find) | The first item for which the lambda is true, or null. |
| [`findIndex`](#findindex) | The position of the first item for which the lambda is true, or -1. |
| [`some`](#some) | Whether the lambda is true for at least one item. |
| [`every`](#every) | Whether the lambda is true for every item. |
| [`none`](#none) | Whether the lambda is false for every item. |
| [`count`](#count) | The number of items, or of items for which the lambda is true. |
| [`flatMap`](#flatmap) | Transforms each item and flattens list results one level. |
| [`reduce`](#reduce) | Folds a list into one value: reduce(list, (acc, item) => ..., initial). |
| [`sort`](#sort) | Sorts numbers, text, timestamps, or durations; pass "desc" to reverse. |
| [`sortBy`](#sortby) | Sorts by a key; pass "desc" to reverse. Nulls sort first. |
| [`groupBy`](#groupby) | Groups items into a map of lists by a key. |
| [`reverse`](#reverse) | The items in reverse order. |
| [`unique`](#unique) | The items without duplicates (by value), in first-seen order. |
| [`flat`](#flat) | Flattens nested lists one level. |
| [`first`](#first) | The first item, or null. |
| [`last`](#last) | The last item, or null. |
| [`join`](#join) | Joins items into text with a separator (default ","). |
| [`slice`](#slice) | A section of text or a list; negative positions count from the end. |
| [`at`](#at) | The item or character at a position; negative positions count from the end. |
| [`includes`](#includes) | Whether text contains a substring, or a list contains a value. |
| [`indexOf`](#indexof) | Position of the first match, or -1. |
| [`lastIndexOf`](#lastindexof) | Position of the last match, or -1. |
| [`isEmpty`](#isempty) | Whether a list, text, or map has no items; null is empty. |
| [`min`](#min) | The smallest value (nulls are skipped); null for an empty list. |
| [`max`](#max) | The largest value (nulls are skipped); null for an empty list. |
| [`sum`](#sum) | The sum of the numbers in a list (nulls are skipped). |
| [`avg`](#avg) | The mean of the numbers in a list (nulls are skipped); null for no numbers. |

## map

Transforms each item.

- `map(T[], (T, number) => U): U[]`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.map(.name) // => ["Pen", "Book", "Bag"]
items.map((it, i) => `${i + 1}. ${it.name}`) // => ["1. Pen", "2. Book", "3. Bag"]
```

## filter

Keeps the items for which the lambda is true.

- `filter(T[], (T, number) => boolean): T[]`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.filter(.price > 5).map(.name) // => ["Book", "Bag"]
```

## find

The first item for which the lambda is true, or null.

- `find(T[], (T, number) => boolean): T | null`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.find(.price > 10) // => { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }
items.find(.price > 100) // => null
```

## findIndex

The position of the first item for which the lambda is true, or -1.

- `findIndex(T[], (T, number) => boolean): number`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.findIndex(.name == "Bag") // => 2
```

## some

Whether the lambda is true for at least one item.

- `some(T[], (T, number) => boolean): boolean`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.some(.price > 20) // => true
```

## every

Whether the lambda is true for every item.

- `every(T[], (T, number) => boolean): boolean`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.every(.qty >= 1) // => true
```

## none

Whether the lambda is false for every item.

- `none(T[], (T, number) => boolean): boolean`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.none(.price < 0) // => true
```

## count

The number of items, or of items for which the lambda is true.

- `count(T[]): number`
- `count(T[], (T, number) => boolean): number`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.count() // => 3
items.count(.qty > 1) // => 1
```

## flatMap

Transforms each item and flattens list results one level.

- `flatMap(T[], (T, number) => U[] | U): U[]`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
[1, 2].flatMap([., . * 10]) // => [1, 10, 2, 20]
```

## reduce

Folds a list into one value: reduce(list, (acc, item) => ..., initial).

- `reduce(T[], (U, T) => U, U): U`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.reduce((total, it) => total + it.price * it.qty, 0) // => 48
```

## sort

Sorts numbers, text, timestamps, or durations; pass "desc" to reverse.

- `sort(T[], ("asc" | "desc")?): T[]`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
[3, 1, 2].sort() // => [1, 2, 3]
["b", "a"].sort("desc") // => ["b", "a"]
```

## sortBy

Sorts by a key; pass "desc" to reverse. Nulls sort first.

- `sortBy(T[], (T, number) => K, ("asc" | "desc")?): T[]`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.sortBy(.price, "desc").map(.name) // => ["Bag", "Book", "Pen"]
```

## groupBy

Groups items into a map of lists by a key.

- `groupBy(T[], (T, number) => string | number | boolean): { [key: string]: T[] }`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.groupBy(.qty > 1 ? "bulk" : "single").keys() // => ["bulk", "single"]
[1, 2, 3, 4].groupBy(. % 2 == 0 ? "even" : "odd") // => { odd: [1, 3], even: [2, 4] }
```

## reverse

The items in reverse order.

- `reverse(T[]): T[]`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
[1, 2, 3].reverse() // => [3, 2, 1]
```

## unique

The items without duplicates (by value), in first-seen order.

- `unique(T[]): T[]`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
[1, 2, 1, 3, 2].unique() // => [1, 2, 3]
[{ a: 1 }, { a: 1 }].unique() // => [{ a: 1 }]
```

## flat

Flattens nested lists one level.

- `flat(any[]): any[]`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
[[1, 2], [3], 4].flat() // => [1, 2, 3, 4]
```

## first

The first item, or null.

- `first(T[]): T | null`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.first().name // => "Pen"
```

## last

The last item, or null.

- `last(T[]): T | null`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->

## join

Joins items into text with a separator (default ",").

- `join((string | number | boolean | null | timestamp | duration)[], string?): string`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
items.map(.name).join(", ") // => "Pen, Book, Bag"
[1, 2, 3].join() // => "1,2,3"
```

## slice

A section of text or a list; negative positions count from the end.

- `slice(T[], number, number?): T[]`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
[1, 2, 3, 4].slice(1, 3) // => [2, 3]
[1, 2, 3, 4].slice(-2) // => [3, 4]
```

## at

The item or character at a position; negative positions count from the end.

- `at(T[], number): T | null`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
[1, 2, 3].at(-1) // => 3
[1, 2, 3].at(5) // => null
```

## includes

Whether text contains a substring, or a list contains a value.

- `includes(T[], any): boolean`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai
[1, 2, 3].includes(2) // => true
[{ id: 1 }].includes({ id: 1 }) // => true
```

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->

## lastIndexOf

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->

Whether a list, text, or map has no items; null is empty.

- `isEmpty(any[] | string | { [key: string]: any } | null): boolean`

<!-- context: { items: [{ name: "Pen", price: 2, qty: 3 }, { name: "Book", price: 12, qty: 1 }, { name: "Bag", price: 30, qty: 1 }] } -->
```bonsai

```
